dante1.text: And thence we came forth to see again the stars.
dante1.author: Dante Alighieri

dante2.text: The Love which moves the sun and the other stars.
dante2.author: Dante Alighieri

leopardi1.text: What are you doing, moon, up in the sky? Tell me, what are you doing, silent moon?
leopardi1.author: Giacomo Leopardi

leopardi2.text: Lovely stars of the Bear, I did not think I would return again, as I used to, to gaze upon you…
leopardi2.author: Giacomo Leopardi

pascoli.text: Saint Lawrence, I know why so many stars burn and fall through the tranquil air…
pascoli.author: Giovanni Pascoli

galileo1.text: Philosophy is written in this grand book… (I mean the universe).
galileo1.author: Galileo Galilei

galileo2.text: The Galaxy is nothing else but a mass of innumerable stars planted together in clusters.
galileo2.author: Galileo Galilei

hack.text: We are the result of stellar evolution; we are made of the matter of the stars.
hack.author: Margherita Hack

copernicus.text: In the middle of all sits the Sun. Who, in this most beautiful temple, would place this lamp in a better place?
copernicus.author: Nicolaus Copernicus

kepler.text: I measured the skies, now the shadows I measure. Skybound was the mind, earthbound the body rests.
kepler.author: Johannes Kepler

ptolemy.text: I know that I am mortal and ephemeral, but when I search out the spirals of the stars my feet no longer touch the earth.
ptolemy.author: Ptolemy

ovid.text: He gave to man an uplifted face and bade him contemplate the heavens and raise his gaze straight to the stars.
ovid.author: Ovid

kant.text: The starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.
kant.author: Immanuel Kant

pascal.text: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces frightens me.
pascal.author: Blaise Pascal

hugo.text: There is one spectacle grander than the sea: the sky; there is one spectacle grander than the sky: the interior of the soul.
hugo.author: Victor Hugo

wilde.text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
wilde.author: Oscar Wilde

vanGogh1.text: I know nothing with any certainty, but the sight of the stars always makes me dream.
vanGogh1.author: Vincent van Gogh

vanGogh2.text: I have a terrible need of — shall I say the word? — religion. Then I go out at night to paint the stars.
vanGogh2.author: Vincent van Gogh

saintExupery1.text: I wonder whether the stars are lit up so that one day each of us may find our own again.
saintExupery1.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

saintExupery2.text: If you love a flower that lives on a star, it is sweet to look at the sky at night. All the stars are a-bloom with flowers.
saintExupery2.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

einstein1.text: The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious.
einstein1.author: Albert Einstein

einstein2.text: The eternally incomprehensible thing about the world is its comprehensibility.
einstein2.author: Albert Einstein

hubble.text: Equipped with his five senses, man explores the universe around him and calls the adventure Science.
hubble.author: Edwin Hubble

feynman.text: I, too, can see the stars on a desert night, and feel them. But do I see less or more?
feynman.author: Richard Feynman

sagan1.text: We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
sagan1.author: Carl Sagan

sagan2.text: The Earth is a very small stage in a vast cosmic arena.
sagan2.author: Carl Sagan

rubin.text: Still other mysteries of the universe remain hidden. Their discovery awaits the adventurous scientists of the future.
rubin.author: Vera Rubin

hawking.text: Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet.
hawking.author: Stephen Hawking

tyson.text: The universe is under no obligation to make sense to you.
tyson.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
